- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days of falling prices, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-adjusted values.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.0–1.0), model exhibits erratic behavior; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85) to reduce forecast amplitude.
